Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run chase. The players and the umpires are back on the ground. Brandon King and Evin Lewis are the two openers for the Men in Maroon. It will be the spin of Mujeeb Ur Rahman to start with the ball for Afghanistan. Here we go!
…THE RUN CHASE…

Ibrahim Zadran is in for a chat. He says that Rasooli was excellent and he played proper cricketing shots without trying too hard. Drawing on his experience, he adds the importance of carrying momentum into the middle overs by rotating the strike and punishing loose deliveries. He says that the total of 181 is good, and says that the focus now shifts to executing their plans with the ball and in the field.

West Indies, meanwhile, looked rusty in the field, with several dropped chances and misfields proving costly. Jayden Seales and Matthew Forde picked up a wicket apiece, while Gudakesh Motie impressed with a tight spell. Chasing 182 for victory, the West Indies will need a strong and composed batting effort. Who do you back to take a 1–0 lead in the series? Stay tuned for the second essay.

A superb batting performance from Afghanistan propelled them to an imposing 181/3 in their 20 overs. After opting to bat first, the Afghans were in early trouble at 19/2, with Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Sediqullah Atal back in the pavilion. Ibrahim Zadran and Darwish Rasooli then steadied the innings, taking their time initially before shifting gears after the halfway mark. The duo stitched together a commanding 162-run partnership for the third wicket. Zadran remained unbeaten on a classy 87, while Rasooli fell on the final ball of the innings after a well-crafted 84. A blistering finish, 70 runs in the last six overs, pushed Afghanistan past the 180-run mark.

OUT! TAKEN! Finally, the West Indies have taken the catch. Slower, back of the hand delivery, around off. Darwish Rasooli miscues the pull toward deep mid-wicket, where Shimron Hetmyer takes the catch. Afghanistan finish on 181/3.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! Afghanistan look to steady the ship. After a shaky start losing two early wickets, one to a sharp run-out and another to a strike from Jayden Seales, Darwish Rasooli and Ibrahim Zadran have done well to rebuild the innings. The partnership is growing, and Ibrahim is looking solid as he inches closer to his half-century. West Indies will hunt for wickets. Let's see ow it pans out...

On the other hand, the West Indies arrive without a few of their first-choice players due to other commitments, with Brandon King taking charge as captain. Squad players such as Quentin Sampson and Shamar Springer will also be eager to make an impact if given the opportunity. So, who will draw first blood in this series? We’ll find out shortly. Led by Rashid Khan, Afghanistan boast match-winners throughout their lineup. Ibrahim Zadran, Sediqullah Atal, and Rahmanullah Gurbaz will be key at the top of the order, while the all-round quartet of Gulbadin Naib, Azmatullah Omarzai, Mohammad Nabi, and Shahidullah Kamal adds depth and balance. With the ball, Rashid will spearhead a formidable attack alongside Mujeeb ur Rahman, Noor Ahmad, and Fazalhaq Farooqi. Overall, the Afghans look like a well-rounded unit and will be keen to get off to a winning start.

Hello everyone, and a very warm welcome to our coverage of the first T20I of the three-match series between Afghanistan and the West Indies, from the Dubai International Stadium. With the T20 World Cup just around the corner, both sides will be eager to fine-tune their combinations and sharpen their preparations ahead of the marquee event.
…MATCHDAY…

The 3-match T20 International series between Afghanistan and the West Indies serves as a vital dress rehearsal for both teams ahead of the T20 World Cup in February. Afghanistan, led by the astute Rashid Khan, will look to leverage their formidable spin attack, featuring Mujeeb Ur Rahman and Noor Ahmad, to exploit the turning tracks in Dubai, a key aspect of their strategy. The onus will be on openers Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmanullah Gurbaz to lay a solid foundation, though the middle order will need to demonstrate greater consistency to ensure competitive totals. To succeed, Afghanistan's batting unit must adeptly navigate the West Indies' pace battery, setting up their spinners to defend. The West Indies, captained by Brandon King, boast a dynamic batting lineup, featuring power-hitters Evin Lewis and Shimron Hetmyer, alongside emerging talents like Quentin Sampson. Their strength lies in this potent batting firepower and a diverse bowling attack, led by Shamar Joseph's pace and Gudakesh Motie's spin. However, the absence of key players and the lack of match practice for some returning from injury could prove a stumbling block. To clinch the series, the West Indies will need their returning players to hit the ground running and effectively counter Afghanistan's spin threat in conditions similar to those at the World Cup venues.
